lore.text: Personal note filed under names-in-copper: A dismissed engineer still signs repair orders through the shared identity MOTH. Someone has crossed out the word inevitable. No replacement was supplied.

evidence.title: Names in Copper / Evidence case
evidence.question: Which explanation fits all three signed records?
clues: Repair order 17 carries the signature of a dismissed engineer.
The same signature appears on MOTH relay packets.
The engineer’s physical badge was destroyed before those packets were sent.

answers.title: The records disagree because of an ordinary clerical error.
answers.feedback: A clerical error does not explain the matching signed authorizations and their order.

answers.title: A lone outsider forged every record after the event.
answers.feedback: The independent receipt and earlier signatures rule out a single later forgery.

answers.title: MOTH is a shared relay identity rather than one physical operator.
answers.feedback: A dismissed engineer still signs repair orders through the shared identity MOTH.
